question: For the Toggle MFA post-pod action, which pod identity configurations are eligible, and is IDM supported?

result.question: For the Toggle MFA post-pod action, which pod identity configurations are eligible, and is IDM supported?
result.answer:
Before you start, note these restrictions from the cited documentation:
> 1. PipelineHub will have a post pod action Enable/Disable MFA and based on the user choice the post pod action will call the corresponding JC's on the IdentityService or IdentityService/ManagedDatabase pods only , this feature is not available for IDM and the UI should not show this feature for IDM PODs. [doc-0098]

Documented guidance:
- The Toggle MFA post-pod action is available only for IdentityService and IdentityService/ManagedDatabase pods. [doc-0098]
- The Toggle MFA feature is explicitly not supported for IDM pods, and the UI must not display this option for them. [doc-0098]
- When MFA is disabled, users can log in to IdentityService and IdentityService/ManagedDatabase pods using only a username and password. [doc-0098]
- If MFA is enabled, users are prompted for extra authentication to log in to the eligible pods. [doc-0098]
- BuildAcceptanceTests automatically disable MFA on the pod during their run, regardless of user settings. [doc-0098]

Sources:
- [doc-0098] PipelineHub Preflight - Post Pod Actions - Toggle MFA

Links, commands, and configurations in this adapted documentation are illustrative.

retrieved_sources.title: PipelineHub Preflight - Post Pod Actions - Toggle MFA
retrieved_sources.text:
Toggle MFA (Multi-Factor Authentication) 

1. PipelineHub will have a post pod action Enable/Disable MFA and based on the user choice the post pod action will call the corresponding JC's on the IdentityService or IdentityService/ManagedDatabase pods only , this feature is not available for IDM and the UI should not show this feature for IDM PODs.
2. if MFA is disabled then the users will be able to login with user name and password on the IdentityService and IdentityService/ManagedDatabase pods
3. if the MFA is enabled user will be prompted for extra authentication to be able to login to the PODs
4. if BuildAcceptanceTests are triggered, BuildAcceptanceTests will automatically disable the MFA on the POD as BuildAcceptanceTests cannot run with MFA on, so when BuildAcceptanceTests are triggered the assumption is that MFA will be disabled (this will be done during the BuildAcceptanceTests run) , irrespective of what the user has done during prov or post prov action.

Eligible PODS (IdentityService) will have the option in the post pod actions - TOGGLE MFA

The user will be able to ENABLE MFA or DISABLE MFA based on the option selected (true or false)

retrieved_sources.title: PipelineHub Preflight - Post Pod Actions - Granular SSH
retrieved_sources.text:
Redcontent moved to DocumentationPortal <https://docs.example.com/reference/resource-673>

Purpose
-------

Use the \***Granular SSH**\* post-pod action to grant SSH access to the users contained in approved Granular SSH groups. Instead of selecting individual users during the action, you select one or more pre-defined groups associated with the target pod's Line of Business (LOB).

Prerequisites
-------------

* Granular SSH groups are LOB-specific. The action lists only groups associated with the target pod's LOB.
* You can select a maximum of \***three groups**\* in one Granular SSH post-pod action.
* **ROLE_GRANULAR_SSH_USER_MANAGEMENT** role is required to create and manage these groups. Ensure the needed groups already exist before submitting the pod action.

Submit a Granular SSH post-pod action
-------------------------------------

1. Open the PipelineHub post-pod action flow for the target pod.
2. Select **Granular SSH** as the post-pod action.
3. Review the groups presented by PIPELINEHUB.

PipelineHub shows groups associated with the target pod's LOB. If a required group is absent, do not substitute an unrelated group; verify the target LOB and group configuration first.
4. Select the group or groups that contain the intended SSH users.

retrieved_sources.title: CloudPlatform EnvironmentService Preflight Submission and Monitoring
retrieved_sources.text:
* When provisioning a POD, please make sure that you understand the "Stack", "Identity", "Database Type" and "Architecture" ahead of time to use

 

### EnvironmentService Stack Options (PreProduction vs PreProd)

EnvironmentService PreProduction stack is inside corporate network and it connects to ArtifactService development zone.  Preflights support is only in PreProduction stack. 99% of Family pods are created in PREPRODUCTION.  

PreProd stack is setup similar to production and its configured to ArtifactService production zone. This is to be used only for special cases where teams need to test their functionality outside corporate network.

Key differences -

* BusinessApp Release sets are created specific for each stack
* Quota requests are handled separately
* Teams will need to request separate cloudnative fleets for PreProduction and PREPROD.  PipelineHub support is in region-a for BusinessApp Monolith so the fleet must be in the same region in OC1
* Service team will also need to set up separate tenancy for this.
* The default options for Identity and Database Types might vary based on the Stack of the POD selected
* Feature flags may vary between the stacks. New feature flags are first introduced in PreProduction and then defaulted in PREPROD to get prepared for PROD.
	+ For example, PreProduction may default to Exa Database and IDM Identity, while PreProd might default to ADBS Database and IdentityService Identity
	+ Therefore, if you plan to use PreProd, please check the landing page for any Banners and special configurations
